developer-tooling.title: Expose Arbiter as an MCP server
developer-tooling.description: Wrap the existing arbiter console script in a Model Context Protocol server so an agent can call scan, gate and review-queue generation as tools, instead of a human typing CLI commands. The server shells out to the console script registered at pyproject.toml:22 rather than importing the package, because src/arbiter/__init__.py exports only __version__ and run_scan takes twelve-plus parameters: the stable Python API should be shaped by observed MCP usage rather than guessed at first. Chosen over a hosted API because hosting requires customer source to leave their machine, which contradicts the offline and ci profiles that declare network False, and because a hosted offering is the one distribution scenario docs/licensing.md marks as needing counsel. Note that MCP relocates the installation rather than removing it -- Arbiter still runs where the repository is on disk.
acceptance_criteria: a tool for scan that takes a path and returns the report json
a tool for gate that returns pass or fail with the claim ledger
a tool that generates a review queue but cannot record a verdict
the offline profile is the default and network is never enabled implicitly
output is written only beneath a caller-specified directory
the server never executes the scanned repository
tests cover the tool schemas and the refusal to mark verdicts
risk_notes: recording verdicts through an automated caller would destroy the calibration ledger's value as the one human-generated signal; the review tool must generate queues only
an MCP dependency is the first new runtime dependency beyond PyYAML and needs a decision on whether it is optional
scanning through a server re-raises the arbiter-out self-contamination defect if callers point output inside the scanned tree

legal.title: Establish licensing terms for arbiter
legal.description: pyproject.toml declares a proprietary licence but the repository carries no LICENSE file and no copyright notice so no terms are granted in writing. docs/licensing.md records the requirements the instrument must satisfy and the questions that block drafting it.
acceptance_criteria: a LICENSE file exists at the repository root and pyproject.toml references it
ownership of scan output is assigned to the user
the redistribution review for bundled analyzers is recorded in NOTICE.md with a date and a reviewer
risk_notes: Requires qualified legal review and cannot be completed by engineering alone
the air-gapped bundle roadmap item stays blocked until the semgrep LGPL-2.1 redistribution question is answered
